overview: White develops the knight before committing the other pieces. The usual game runs 3...Nf6 4.Nc3, then Black chooses the Pure Slav with ...dxc4 or the Semi-Slav with ...e6. In the Pure Slav Black gets the c8 bishop outside the pawn chain and tries to hold or return the c4 pawn, while White grabs the centre with e3 or e4.

white_ideas.idea: Win back the c4 pawn with a4 and e3, keeping a small space edge.
Build a centre with e4 if Black overextends on the queenside.

black_ideas.idea: Get the light bishop out with ...Bf5 or ...Bg4 before ...e6.
Hold the pawn with ...b5 or return it and break with ...e5 or ...c5.

typical_structures.structure: Pure Slav: Black c6 and d-pawn traded for c4, White e3 and d4 centre.
Semi-Slav triangle c6-d5-e6 if Black plays ...e6.

character.notes: Pure Slav is sound and hard to break down; the Semi-Slav branches are sharp but the line itself stays Solid.

gambit.notes: dxc4 pawn is won back by force or returned.

structure.notes: Queen's pawn centre with tension; after exchanges one half-open c-file. Semi-open.

level.notes: Main lines have theory but the Pure Slav is playable with plans. Intermediate.

plan_phrases: good light bishop outside the chain

sublines_that_differ.name: Semi-Slav
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. Nc3 e6
sublines_that_differ.how: Theory heavy and often sharp (Botvinnik, Meran).

sublines_that_differ.name: Slav-Reti System
sublines_that_differ.how: Fianchetto with a slower, flexible game.

character.reason: The Slav is known as hard to break down, with few early tactics.

gambit.reason: The c4 pawn comes back by force.

structure.reason: Exchanges leave a half-open c-file; the QGD family is Semi-open per the anchors.

level.reason: Plans are clear but the branches need theory.

plans.reason: Black or White uses the c-file after the exchanges.
